en: The Thirteen-Book Collection of Birth Stories (Jātaka),
Chapter on Mangoes (Ambavagga)
3. The Jātaka of the Swift Swan “Alight right here, O swan;
your sight is dear to me.”
"You have attained lordship;
declare what there is here.
"Through hearing alone, people become dear to one,"
But having seen him, desire arises in one person;
having both seen and heard him, they become dear.
Perhaps you find pleasure in seeing me?
You are dear to me by hearing of you,
and even more so by coming to see you;
thus, you are one whose sight is dear to me.
“Dwell, O swan, in my presence.
“We would dwell in your house,
always honored and revered.”
And once, being intoxicated, I thought:
"Let them cook the king of swans for me.
Fie on that drinking of liquor!
"Even that which is dearer to me than you,
I shall not drink liquor as long as you dwell in my house."
“The cries of jackals and the calls of birds, O King, as well as the speech of humans, are easy to understand.”
It is even more difficult to recognize than that:
even if a person considers someone as a relative, a friend, or a companion.
He who, having been cheerful before,
later becomes otherwise;
in whom the mind settles—
He is far away even though he is nearby,
and he is near even though he is far,
if the mind does not enter into him.
He may have a mind full of faith within,
with a mind full of faith on the further shore of the ocean;
yet he may also have a mind that is corrupt within.
O bull among charioteers, those who dwell together in the same direction but live apart with defiled hearts are as far from one another as the further shore of the ocean.
The virtuous dwell together in harmony through their minds,
O increaser of the kingdom;
yet by dwelling too long, [conflict arises].
One who was dear becomes not dear;
let us go and bid you farewell before we become those who are no longer dear to you.
“If you do not acknowledge the salutation with joined palms of these hundreds of attendants who are thus entreating you, [what will you do when you are entreated by those who have come from afar?]”
"You do not carry out our word;
thus we entreat you:
please act upon this request once more."
“If we dwell in this way,
no obstacle shall arise;
and for you too, O Great King.”
And may we see Raṭṭhavaḍḍhana as well,
at the passing of days and nights.”
The Third Jātaka: The Javanahamsa Jātaka.
